overall: Tomorrow (June 6) in Atlanta is expected to be a warm early-summer day with a significant temperature rise from today's observed high of 71.6°F. The ensemble model projects a daily maximum around 82-83°F, suggesting seasonably warm but not extreme conditions. Overall confidence in the forecast is low, as both prediction tiers are flagged Tier 4.
forecast_obs_notes: Model agreement is poor, with notable divergence on the upper temperature range: GFS is a notable warm outlier at 22% for the 90-91°F bucket, while NBM assigns 0% to that same bucket and ECMWF (7%) and HRRR (4%) remain skeptical. This spread signals meaningful forecast uncertainty and reduces confidence in any single outcome.
max_temp_prediction: The ensemble expected TMAX of 82.8°F is the most reliable anchor given the low and scattered bucket probabilities — no single bucket exceeds 19% probability. The 90-91°F range promoted by GFS appears to be an outlier unsupported by the broader model consensus, and the ~11°F jump from today's 71.6°F observed high adds further skepticism to the high-end scenarios. Confidence is low overall; the most defensible estimate clusters near the ensemble mean of ~82-83°F.
